data.title: GEOPOLITICS | Bessent Faces Questions at Carlyle Global Investor Conference
data.description:
Dani Burger is at Carlyle's Global Investor Conference discussing defense tech, AI and the outlook for credit with Ian Fujiyama, Jason Thomas and Alex Chi, according to Bloomberg.

The program also covers pressure on the Federal Reserve, questions about an AI slowdown and Scott Bessent's Capitol Hill appearance on inflation, energy and AI.

data.title: Apple AirPods 5 Add Noise Cancellation at $129
data.description:
Apple’s AirPods 5 start at $129 and add noise cancellation, with improved sound, according to Bloomberg.

The article says it is worth paying an extra $20 for wireless charging and volume controls, but both versions of the AirPods 5 offer better sound and noise cancellation.

data.title: AI | OpenAI Seeks Canada Data Center Partnerships Under Carney
data.description:
OpenAI Inc. is looking at Canada for data center partnerships under Prime Minister Mark Carney, according to Bloomberg.

One of OpenAI's top executives, who previously hired Carney to lead the Bank of England, said the company is taking a close look at the country.

data.title: Cramer Says S&P 500 Declines Accelerated as 10-Year Treasury Yield Hit Highest Since 2007
data.description: According to CNBC, the S&P 500's declines accelerated Tuesday after the 10-year Treasury yield reached its highest level since 2007, while oil also rallied. Jim Cramer said investors were focusing on the wrong drivers of the market and pointed to the surge in bond yields, the rise in oil and concerns about what could happen if the Federal Reserve raises interest rates Wednesday. The CME FedWatch tool showed odds of a rate hike above 92%. Cramer also warned against trying to forecast several rate moves ahead, saying that approach is a "parlor game." Separately, shares of Intel and Micron were modestly higher after Monday's sharp declines tied to Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei's weekend letter calling for a slowdown in artificial intelligence development over safety concerns. Cramer said he still views Intel and Micron as buys and said the portfolio added a few shares of Micron on Monday after the semiconductor group stabilized.

data.title: GEOPOLITICS | Bessent Pushes Back on Treasury Bond-Market Intervention Criticism
data.description: US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent defended the Treasury’s recent intervention in the bond market after US Representative Jim Himes, a Connecticut Democrat, questioned the move and said it distorts free markets, according to Bloomberg.

data.title: Judge Blocks Kennedy Center Board From Honoring Trump With Name Inscription
data.description: According to CNBC, a federal judge on Tuesday blocked the John F. Kennedy Center for the Performing Arts board from inscribing President Donald Trump's name on the center's main building and from naming the campus after him. U.S. District Judge Christopher Cooper said the board cannot install memorials for Trump or anyone else at the Kennedy Center without Congress's approval, after the board renewed its push to place Trump's name on official markers despite an earlier ruling that it could not add him to the center's official name. The board had approved an Aug. 13 resolution to honor Trump's future contributions to the center and planned to add an inscription reading, "The John F. Kennedy Memorial Center for the Performing Arts," with the words "renovated and restored by President Donald J. Trump" underneath, as well as rename the grounds "The President Donald J. Trump Plaza." Both actions had been set for Sept. 8 before the board extended the deadline to Oct. 8. The Department of Justice argued that blocking the moves could deter donors and leave the center short of funds for renovations.

data.title: Fannie Mae And Freddie Mac Expand Mortgage Credit Score Options
data.description:
According to CNBC, Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac are now allowing lenders to use VantageScore 4.0, in addition to the classic FICO score, for all mortgages sold to the government-sponsored enterprises. The change expands a limited rollout announced in April and follows a Sept. 3 post on X from Bill Pulte, director of the Federal Housing Finance Agency, which oversees the two mortgage buyers.

VantageScore 4.0 can factor in data such as rent and utility payments, which may help some borrowers qualify for a mortgage or secure a better rate, experts said. CNBC reported that about a third of mortgage denials for primary home purchases with conventional loans in 2025 were tied to a lack of credit history, according to Zillow's analysis of 2025 Home Mortgage Disclosure Act data.

The article also said FHFA may reduce the number of credit reports lenders must review from three to two, while Pulte said the agency is also studying the use of a single credit report in the mortgage application process. Separately, the Federal Housing Administration will begin insuring mortgages underwritten with VantageScore 4.0 and FICO 10T on Jan. 1.

data.title: Jim Cramer’s Charitable Trust Buys 80 More Shares of Bank of New York
data.description:
According to CNBC, Jim Cramer’s Charitable Trust is buying 80 shares of Bank of New York at roughly $153, lifting its total holding to 320 shares and increasing the trust’s weighting to about 1.25% from 0.95%. The trust started a small position two weeks ago and is adding after the stock fell about 5.5% over the past two sessions.

Bank of New York Chief Financial Officer Dermot McDonogh said at the Barclays Global Financial Services Conference that third-quarter revenue was a little slower than the seasonally stronger second quarter, but remained within management’s guidance from the end of the second quarter. He also said volumes in the capital markets business were strong and had picked back up in September, reiterated the bank’s 6%-7% full-year expense outlook, and said the company remains committed to delivering positive operating leverage again next year.

data.title: David Rubenstein Warns U.S. Debt Is a "Ticking Time Bomb"
data.description:
Carlyle Group co-founder and billionaire investor David Rubenstein warned that the United States' expanding debt is like a ticking time bomb and said it is weakening national security. According to Sina Finance, he said the U.S. now carries $40 trillion in debt and that annual interest costs have already exceeded defense spending.

Rubenstein made the remarks in a recent podcast episode. He said annual interest expense is now slightly above $1 trillion, while the defense budget is also about $1 trillion.

According to Sina Finance, DoubleLine's latest analysis showed that annual U.S. debt interest payments have risen to a record 18.5% of federal revenue, breaking the previous 18.4% high set in 1991. The report also said annual interest expense has reached a record $1.25 trillion, more than four times the 1991 level.

Rubenstein said the result is higher interest rates, which would raise the cost of mortgages, ordinary borrowing, and credit card use.

data.title: House Committee to Consider Crypto Tax Bill Exempting Fees of $10 or Less
data.description:
The House Ways and Means Committee will consider legislation that would exempt qualifying crypto network or transaction fees of $10 or less from capital-gains calculations. According to NS3.AI, the markup is scheduled for Wednesday at 10 a.m. Eastern on Sept. 16.

The bill would also set tax rules for stablecoins, staking, mining and digital asset trading. It still needs to pass Congress and receive the President's approval before it can become law.

data.title: Amazon Unable to Restore Some Data After Persian Gulf Facility Damage
data.description: Amazon.com Inc. has been unable to restore access to some data stored at Persian Gulf facilities damaged during the US-Iran war, according to Bloomberg.

data.title: Anthropic Says It Was Profitable For A Second Straight Quarter
data.description: Anthropic told investors it was profitable for a second straight quarter, though the figure excludes the cost of building the next version of Claude, according to BeInCrypto, citing the Financial Times. The company also said adjusted operating income was positive again and gross margins topped 80%, but those margins exclude Amazon’s cut and model-training costs. Revenue reached $11.5 billion in the second quarter, 14 times a year earlier, as markets await Anthropic’s planned Nasdaq listing.

data.title: DoubleLine Capital's Jeffrey Sherman Says the Fed Needs to Raise Rates
data.description: According to Wallstreetcn, DoubleLine Capital Deputy Chief Investment Officer Jeffrey Sherman said the Federal Reserve needs to raise rates to convince traders it is committed to lowering inflation and ease market concerns that pushed 10-year U.S. Treasury yields above 5% this week. Sherman said Fed Governor Kevin Warsh has the ability to help by raising rates as soon as tomorrow, and added that the market is already pricing in a rate hike.

data.title: Iran's Foreign Minister Araghchi Says Claims That Iran Is Defenseless Are False
data.description: According to Wallstreetcn, Iran's Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said claims that Iran is defenseless are false, adding that U.S. Defense Department messages said hundreds of U.S. military facilities were blown to pieces and dozens of military aircraft were burned, and that this was only the tip of the iceberg.

data.title: GEOPOLITICS | Radiant World, Sapphire Minmetals Sue Glencore in Singapore for $2 Billion
data.description: Radiant World and Sapphire Minmetals have filed a lawsuit against Glencore Plc in Singapore seeking $2 billion in damages, according to a senior executive at the group of companies, Bloomberg reported.

data.title: Bond Traders Price In Fed Rate Hike on Wednesday
data.description: Bond traders are pricing in a Federal Reserve interest-rate hike on Wednesday with a level of conviction that has proven right for decades, according to Bloomberg.

data.title: Brookfield Nears Center Parcs Recapitalization at $6 Billion Valuation
data.description: Brookfield is nearing a recapitalization of Center Parcs in a deal that values the British holiday park operator at about $6 billion, people familiar with the matter said, according to Bloomberg.

data.title: STOCKS | RBC Capital Markets Upgrades ResMed to Outperform
data.description:
ResMed shares rose nearly 5% on Tuesday after RBC Capital Markets upgraded the medical device and digital health company from Sector Perform to Outperform. According to Sina Finance, the firm also raised its price target to $262 from $244, implying 17% upside from the current share price of $229.

RBC Capital Markets cited ResMed's improving earnings outlook and stronger capital management as the main reasons for the upgrade. The firm said ResMed could deliver high-single-digit earnings growth over the next several years.

data.title: UK Fiscal Watchdog to Issue One Forecast Before Budget
data.description:
Britain’s fiscal watchdog will publish just one economic forecast before the Treasury sets budget policy, according to a person familiar with the matter.

The change is intended to make the process more predictable and give the Chancellor of the Exchequer more time to prepare, Bloomberg reported.

data.title: U.S. Treasury Says Bond Buyback Intervention Was Successful, Discusses AI Liability and Japan Intervention
data.description:
The U.S. Treasury said its bond buyback intervention was successful and that a funding offset plan for $5,000 checks is moving forward. According to Odaily, it also said it would meet House Speaker Johnson if congressional authorization is clearly needed, and urged lawmakers not to exempt artificial intelligence companies from liability.

The Treasury said AI policy must address both innovation and safety, and that companies should not receive a blank check on liability. It also said it is engaged in ongoing discussions about Japan intervention, used a notional amount in yen intervention, and earned tens of millions of dollars from that intervention. The Treasury added that it previously earned tens of millions of dollars from aid provided to Argentina.
